subject: Equinox POC: runbook, success metrics, and burst capacity plan
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Gupta <samir@equinox.ai>
Cc: Priya Singh <priya.singh@equinox.ai>
Date: Mon, 1 Nov 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Post-demo recap + POC runbook ask

Hi Samir — thanks again for the demo this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned while we scope the POC.

Recap (what we heard)
- Goal: validate that Redwood inference can provision steady-state throughput for your document-summarization endpoint (avg latency < 300ms, 99th < 750ms) and reduce token cost vs your current setup by >= 25%.
- Data: 250k documents (varied sizes), primary test set = 10k real documents you'll supply (sample agreed on call).
- Security: needs SOC2 evidence + VPC peering or Private deployment option for any sensitive files.

Ask: to finalize the runbook we need the following from you by EOD Friday 11/5:
1) Confirm success criteria (latency, quality thresholds, cost targets) — short bullets fine.
2) Share the 10k sample, or a link to where we'll pull it.
3) Expected concurrent sessions and peak request pattern (e.g., steady 50 req/s with 5-minute bursts up to 250 req/s).

What we’ll deliver from Redwood
- Draft POC runbook (timeline, ownership, acceptance gates)
- GPU sizing recommendation and reserved capacity proposal (estimates for reserved GPUs + burst policy)
- Monitoring hooks and eval plan (prompt set, accuracy/ROUGE thresholds, throughput testing steps)

Attached a one-page template (equinox_poc_template.xlsx) to capture URLs, sample dataset access, and the initial success criteria — please fill the highlighted fields.

Proposed timeline
- Confirm sample & criteria by 11/5
- Kickoff + infra reservation week of 11/8
- 2-week evaluation window (11/15–11/29) with acceptance review the week of 11/29
If that looks good I’ll loop in Karthik from infra to propose exact GPU counts and autoscaling details.
Thanks —
Kimberly Park

Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + POC runbook ask

Thanks Kim — all clear and appreciate the template. Quick answers inline and a couple clarifications: 

Success criteria (confirming)
- Latency: median < 300ms, p95 < 600ms, p99 < 900ms for our 512-token average requests.
- Quality: extractive summary F1 >= 0.78 on your evaluation harness (we’ll share scoring rubric).
- Cost: targeted >20% unit-cost reduction vs current committed infra (we can iterate if your numbers are higher).

Data & access
- Shared a read-only S3 link to the 10k sample (s3://equinox-poc/samples/10k). Link sent to your infra@redwood account.

Traffic profile (expected)
- Steady-state: ~40 rps overall (peak concurrency ~60).
- Burst scenario: monthly marketing surges produce 10–12x for short windows (~3–8 minutes) — plan for controlled bursts to 400–500 rps for up to 8 minutes.
\Constraints and notes
- We need Private deployment/network isolation for any documents flagged PII. SOC2 evidence is required before we move beyond trial.
\Question: can Redwood guarantee that a reserved capacity + autoscaling policy will be able to handle the 10–12x short bursts without request rejection? If not, what graceful degradation behavior do you recommend?
\We’ll aim to confirm the template by 11/5. Thx — Samir

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Samir Gupta <samir@equinox.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 4 Nov 2027 14:26:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Post-demo recap + POC runbook ask (GPU sizing + autoscale proposal)

Hi all — jumping in with the infra plan and recommended runbook items based on the traffic profile Samir provided. High level first, then a short runbook.
Sizing recommendation (initial)
- Baseline (steady-state): reserve 4 x A40-equivalent GPUs (NVIDIA A40 class) to provide consistent latency for 40 rps at your 512-token average and maintain p95 targets with small headroom.
- Burst capacity: configure burst pool of +12 GPUs that can be provisioned via autoscale within a 60–90s window using cold-start warm pools. That gives us headroom for 10–12x short surges (400–500 rps) while keeping steady costs lower.
- Fallback model variants: we’ll provision a quantized model variant with slightly lower quality but faster throughput for automatic fallback if cold pool is exhausted.
Autoscaling policy
- Warm pool: maintain 2 hot standby VMs with GPU attached to reduce cold-start latency to < 30s for incremental scale-ups.
- Scale step: add GPUs in steps of 2 up to burst pool.
- Scale-in policy: aggressive scale-in after 5 minutes below threshold to avoid prolonged cost exposure.
Monitoring and acceptance hooks
- Telemetry: token-level cost, qps, latency (p50/p95/p99), GPU utilization, and KV-cache hit rates.
- Test harness: we’ll run a synthetic ramp (script + load profile) that mirrors your peak burst pattern and verify: no 5xx errors, p95 latency under target for 85% of requests during bursts, and graceful degradation (fallback model invoked) when cold pool is exhausted.
Runbook (POC phases)
1) Kickoff (week of 11/8): infra reservation + VPC peering steps; confirm point-of-contact for troubleshooting (we recommend an on-call window during initial bursts).
2) Integration (11/8–11/12): data access, prompt injection checks, and a dry-run with 5% of your sample.
3) Load & eval (11/15–11/29): run steady-state tests + two scheduled burst simulations (we’ll coordinate exact times), collect metrics, run quality evals.
4) Acceptance review (week of 11/29): compare against agreed thresholds and adjust GPU counts/quant profiles.
Attachments: gpu_sizing_v1.pdf (PDF, 120KB) — includes throughput charts and cost delta estimates.
Answers to Samir’s question on guarantees
- We cannot guarantee zero rejections under an instantaneous, uncontrolled 12x cold surge without pre-warmed capacity, but with the above warm-pool + burst pool plus fallback variants we expect <1% request rejection during scheduled/simulated bursts. For fully uncontrolled production spikes we recommend a short-term scheduled buffer (pre-warm) or a temporary override to increase warm pool prior to predictable marketing events.
Next steps
- Kimberly: confirm kickoff time on 11/8 (30–45m).
- Samir/Priya: confirm who will be the infra POC and share IAM role/email for S3 access (if not already sent).
- I’ll circulate a short infra checklist before kickoff.
— Karthik
